name: gate
wording: A hold point at a handover: the work does not go past it without the operator's sign-off. The gates are a story's read-back, held by the architect; a story's plan read-back, held by the lead, which a task with no story skips unless the operator calls it; a change the operator has asked to review before it joins, held by the lead; release; a fork that is irreversible, about value or beyond the architect's competence; and any point the operator calls, stop included. At a gate its holder, the party whose handover it is, interrupts, unless the sign-off there is delegated. Between gates the agents work without checking in.
reason: The operator: what cratylus delivers assumed one convention, GitHub flow with a branch and a pull request per task, and review of every change whatever its risk; it is generic over a project's conventions, and review follows risk as Ship, Show or Ask. A gate is one of the operator's hold points and nothing else is one, so statements of what is not a gate say nothing.
